goal: Fix search pagination so paging through relevance-sorted results never shows an item twice or skips one.

entries.content: Search results show duplicates on page 2, and some items never appear at all, when paging through results sorted by relevance.
ran: git status — clean working tree on main
read package.json — scripts: dev, build, test, lint; deps include pg, express, zod
ran: ls src — api/, db/, search/, cache/, utils/, index.ts
read README.md — local setup instructions, docker compose for postgres
ran: docker compose up -d — postgres started on 5432
ran: npm install — added 412 packages in 9s
ran: npm test -- search.test.ts — 2 failed: 'page 2 contains item 7 already shown on page 1', 'item 19 never returned across pages'
read src/api/health.ts — health check endpoint returns uptime
grep 'searchItems' src — defined in src/search/query.ts, called from src/search/routes.ts
read src/search/query.ts — SELECT ... ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2, with no secondary sort key
Hypothesis: the cache layer might be serving a stale page 1 while page 2 is fresh.
read src/cache/index.ts — search cache keyed by query + page, TTL 60s
ran: grep TTL config/test.json — cache TTL is 0 in tests, so caching is disabled there
Caching is disabled in tests, so it can't explain the failing test. Ruling out the cache hypothesis.
read docker-compose.yml — postgres 16, redis 7

ran: git show a1b2c3 -- src/search/query.ts — the ranking change replaced ORDER BY created_at, id with ORDER BY score DESC

The ranking change dropped the id tiebreaker. Many items share identical scores, and Postgres doesn't guarantee a stable order for ties across separate LIMIT/OFFSET queries, which explains both the duplicates and the missing items.
